item.title: Man accused of Fort Smith stabbing pleads not guilty
item.description: A man has pleaded not guilty to multiple charges after a March 14 stabbing in Fort Smith left a woman seriously injured.

item.title: WEATHER BLOG: National Weather Service announces nex-gen advances
item.description: The National Weather Service (NWS) is planning to move its data and services to a cloud server and develop new tools to replace current applications, which will increase flexibility and scalability for its offices and partners, and allow for the integration of artificial intelligence and public/private data sources.

item.title: Rogers Retirement Community Celebrates Resident's 100th Birthday
item.description: The Pinnacle Springs Retirement Community in Rogers celebrates a historic milestone for one of their residents.

item.title: Rogers Historical Museum hosts "Spring Break at the Museum: Colonial Days"
item.description: The Rogers Historical Museum launches a year-long celebration of America's 250th anniversary with a specialized spring break program, "Spring Break at the Museum: Colonial Days"

item.title: Arkansas Public Theatre returning to Victory Theater after tornado damage repairs
item.description: ROGERS, Ark. (KNWA/KFTA) — Victory Theater is set to reopen this year, following two years of repairs since sustaining damage from Memorial Day weekend tornadoes in 2024. During those tornadoes, Victory Theater suffered roof damage, as well as water damage inside the building, forcing the City of Rogers to shut the building down for repairs. [...]

item.title: Fort Smith parents learn new drug trends, apps threaten kids
item.description: Parents and law enforcement teamed up to help keep the kids in Fort Smith by hosting a crime prevention class to teach parents about new drug trends and apps posing threats to children and teens.

item.title: Habitat for Humanity helps new homeowner achieve dream
item.description: A Northwest Arkansas resident after months of building, now has her dream home with the help of a local organization.

item.title: Arkansas basketball to play Michigan State in Thanksgiving game in Detroit
item.description: The Razorback men's basketball team will be back in the national spotlight on Thanksgiving Day for another neutral site game.

item.title: University of Arkansas to offer free youth mental health first aid training
item.description: The University of Arkansas Department of Health, Human Performance and Recreation collaborating with Southern Alliance for Youth Mental Health to host a free youth mental health first aid certifications for students, faculty, staff and the NWA community, according to a release.

item.title: Springdale man accused of taking advantage of incompetent person placed in diversion program
item.description: A Springdale man accused of taking advantage of a man with dementia has been placed into a diversion program, according to court documents.

item.title: Bentonville man pleads guilty to insider trading: DOJ
item.description: A Bentonville man has pleaded guilty in an insider trading case where he received a tip from an executive and turned an investment into a nearly 500% profit, according to the Department of Justice.

item.title: WEATHER BLOG: Northwest Arkansas had its warmest March on record
item.description: Arkansas experienced a heat dome in March 2026 that set new temperature records, with Fayetteville having its warmest month on record and Fort Smith having its second warmest March.

item.title: Leflore County man faces charges for shooting police officer
item.description: LeFlore County resident pleads guilty to assault with the intent to commit murder of Webber Falls police officer in March 2025, according to a news release.

item.title: Fort Smith PD warns of convincing scams targeting residents
item.description: The Fort Smith Police Department warns of ongoing scams resulting in significant financial losses and is urging residents to remain vigilant following a recent increase in reports.

item.title: ULI Symposium addresses regional project financing challenges
item.description: Public officials, finance professionals, and others met in Elm Springs for the Urban Land Institute Northwest Arkansas Spring Symposium to address rapid infrastructure growth.
